candidates.title: Manual's Lua access-log format (per-access 'proof' table with target_address/root_hash, 'read'/'written' always 2^log2_size bytes for log2_size>=5) does not match what log_* return and verify_* consume ('sibling_hashes' directly on the access, no 'proof', no data for >=32-byte accesses unless ACCESS_LOG_TYPE_LARGE_DATA)
candidates.component: Lua machine API documentation (doc/README.md 'State-transition proofs') vs log_step_uarch/log_reset_uarch/log_send_cmio_response and the off-chain verify_* functions
candidates.role: Support (off-chain verifiers and their documented log format); the log producers are honest operator, but their output is not wrong, only differently shaped than documented
candidates.location: doc/README.md ~5731-5800 (access_log/access/proof grammar and the 'For accesses at or above ... each field is exactly 2^log2_size bytes long' sentence); src/json-util.cpp access_log to_json/from_json; src/clua-i-machine.cpp AccessLog schema
candidates.description: The manual documents access ::= {type, address, log2_size, read_hash, read, written_hash, written, proof} with proof ::= {target_address, log2_target_size, log2_root_size, target_hash, root_hash, sibling_hashes}, says 'Merkle-tree proofs are always included', and says that for log2_size >= 5 the read/written fields are exactly 2^log2_size bytes. The implementation emits accesses with keys {address, log2_size, type, read_hash, read?, written_hash?, written?, sibling_hashes}: there is no proof sub-table (no target_address/root_hash/target_hash), and for log2_size >= 5 accesses (e.g. the 32-byte revert-root-hash write at 0xfe0 and the rx-buffer write in a delivery log) read and written are omitted entirely unless ACCESS_LOG_TYPE_LARGE_DATA is set. The verifiers read 'sibling_hashes' from the access; a log built in the documented shape (proof.sibling_hashes) is not what they parse.
candidates.trigger: Any integrator or third-party verifier implementation that follows the manual's grammar; no adversary involvement.
candidates.reachability: Always: every log produced by log_send_cmio_response / log_step_uarch / log_reset_uarch has this shape.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion applies (not a deliberate API change, not an untrusted API caller). 2 Role: the documented log format is consumed by the off-chain verify functions, which AUDIT.md rates 'Support'; the referee (Solidity step via prt-ethereum.lua append_log) has its own binary encoding that is not affected. 3 High/Medium: section 8 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' If the manual were right, the producers would emit a different (but equally verifiable) shape; no wrong hash, no accepted wrong transition, no completeness loss for the honest operator, whose own tools use the real shape. No Medium case fits ('A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium' requires a High/Critical in the stood-in role). 4 Critical: no rule or obligation is violated at a reachable state. 5 Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model' (documentation of a support interface).
candidates.threat_to_goal: None directly; it can only make an independent verifier written from the manual reject honest logs (support-only, off-chain).
candidates.evidence: Scratch e1.lua/e2.lua: log_send_cmio_response on the emit-output bare-metal guest, local and via spawn_server: access keys = address,log2_size,read,read_hash,sibling_hashes,type (+written,written_hash for writes); accesses 5 (0xfe0, log2 5) and 6 (0x60000000, log2 5) have no read/written without LARGE_DATA; no 'proof' key on any access. Verification still succeeds (verify_send_cmio_response returns the after-hash).
candidates.test_idea: Lua test: produce log_step_uarch(ACCESS_LOG_TYPE_ANNOTATIONS) and assert every access has a 'proof' table with sibling_hashes, target_address == address, log2_target_size == log2_size, and that for log2_size >= 5 #read == 2^log2_size (exits 1 today); or, if the code is canonical, the fix is to the manual.

candidates.title: Manual says collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes uses <revert_uarch_tail> only when the fixed point is a rejected input, but the implementation refuses every call that may execute a non-fixed-point mcycle (or starts at a rejected yield) without a valid tail
candidates.component: collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes / collect_uarch_cycle_bundle (machine API, Lua binding) vs doc/README.md 'Computation hashes'
candidates.role: Honest operator (collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes per the AUDIT.md table); the discrepancy is in the manual's description
candidates.location: doc/README.md ~5681-5693; src/machine.cpp collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes 2795-2824 ('revert uarch tail is required', 'too short', 'does not end with the revert root hash'); src/cm.h 982-988 documents the stricter rule
candidates.description: The Lua manual describes the third argument as supplying 'the entries of the reverted machine in place of that when the fixed point is a rejected input', implying it is optional and only consulted on rejection. The implementation (and cm.h) requires it before executing anything whenever the machine is not at a fixed point (and whenever it starts at an rx-rejected yield), and additionally requires its last entry to equal the machine's current revert root hash. A caller following the manual gets 'revert uarch tail is required' for every mid-input uarch-level claim, and must first compute the tail on the machine to which the current input was delivered.
candidates.trigger: A trusted caller (operator tooling) written from the Lua manual calls machine:collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes(mcycle+1, b) on a machine in the middle of an input.
candidates.reachability: Any reachable mid-input state. The failure is loud (exception before any state change), never a wrong hash.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: arguably 'a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller' (Low example), but the misuse is what the manual describes, so not excluded. 2 Role: honest operator (collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes). 3 High/Medium: if the manual were right, the call would succeed without a tail when no rejection happens; the code instead fails loudly before changing the machine, and the documented C API (cm.h) states the stricter precondition, so an honest operator built on the C API is unaffected and can always comply (R4 still holds: the tail is computable from the delivered-to machine it already keeps). No wrong hash or unprovable state results. No listed High/Medium case fits. 4 Critical: no rule violated at a reachable state; R4 'can always compute the claim' holds once the precondition is met. 5 Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None: it can only make a manual-following caller fail loudly; the hashes produced when the tail is given match a naive reference.
candidates.evidence: Scratch e8.lua: collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes(mcycle+1, 0) without a tail on a machine at an rx-rejected yield (and earlier on a mid-input machine) raises 'revert uarch tail is required'. Differential e6.lua: with the tail, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes (bundles 0,1,3,7) and collect_uarch_cycle_bundle (offsets 0,1,5,last-1,last) match a naive run_uarch/get_root_hash/reset_uarch reference with the rejection exception, for reject, halt, exception and long-input guests (0 hash mismatches; the only differences are Lua's 1-based mcycle_hash_offsets, which the Lua manual's wording allows).
candidates.test_idea: Lua test on a mid-input machine: call collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes(mcycle+1, 0) without a tail and assert it succeeds when the mcycle does not reject (exits 1 today); or fix the manual to state the precondition.

not_covered: Manual statements for remote machines were checked by reading and a small run (spawn_server, fork_server independence, cleanup-call inheritance, shutdown+swap+rebind to the old address, remote vs local send_cmio_response validation and collect_mcycle_root_hashes); not covered: fork/rebind/shutdown failure injection, client timeouts expiring mid-request (documented as leaving server state unknown), fork of machines whose backing files are later modified by another process, inherited flock descriptors in fork children, remote hosts other than 127.0.0.1, IPv6 addresses.

collect_mcycle_root_hashes was compared with a naive per-mcycle reference only on the emit-output bare-metal guest (periods 2^0..2^3 for short reject/halt/exception inputs and a reject after a long input, 2^17/2^20/2^22 for a 5M-mcycle accepted input; phases 0, P-1, P/2; bundles 0..3; chunked calls with partial bundles; sibling-proof check). Not covered: automatic yields landing exactly on sampling points with bundling across calls on a Linux guest, console_output break reasons, mcycle_overflow (imcyclemax) fixed points, bundle heights above 3, collect_mcycle_bundle.
collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes differential did not cover mcycles whose uarch runs close to 2^20 cycles (the 'execution reached final bundle' branch) or Linux workloads.

Output-proof section: hash_tree.frontier(<last_output_proof>) and frontier_next_proofs were read, not run; the outputs-Merkle-root proof (iflags_Y/htif_tohost/tx-buffer words) was not checked against the rollups contracts.

Rolling-from-storage section: only rename_stored refusal on an existing destination and sync_stored refusal while a SHARING_ALL machine holds the directory were spot-checked; the example's final state hash and crash-recovery naming were not reproduced.

State-transition-proof section: verify_step_uarch error messages and tamper cases were spot-checked on a bare-metal guest (consistent with the manual's examples); the manual's printed dump-uarch-step output on config-nothing-to-do was not reproduced; verify_reset_uarch/verify_send_cmio_response were exercised only on honest logs.
ZK step logs (log_step/verify_step) were not examined (out of scope).
